title: Individual spiced pumpkin pies
subtitle: small pumpkin pies in individual pastry cases
excerpt: Individual spiced pumpkin pies are single-portion versions of the classic American Thanksgiving pie, baked in deep tartlet tins. Each one holds a smooth, warmly spiced pumpkin custard filling in a buttery short pastry shell. Making them individually means crispier pastry per serving and easier serving at dinner parties, no cutting, no serving wedges, just place on the plate.
sourceNotes: Pumpkin pie is the defining American Thanksgiving dessert, with recipes in American cookbooks from the 18th century. The spice blend (cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, cloves) used in pumpkin pie is a standardised American flavour combination that varies relatively little between recipes. Individual pumpkin pies follow the same format in a small tin format. Tinned pumpkin puree (not pumpkin pie filling, which already contains spices and sweetener) is the practical choice for this recipe; fresh pumpkin can be used but requires roasting and pureeing first and tends to produce a wetter, less uniform filling.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze fully cooled, wrapped individually. Defrost in the fridge overnight and serve at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the day before; the filling firms and improves overnight.
recipe.temperatureNote: for the pumpkin custard fill; blind bake cases at 190°C first

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: 160°C conventional (140°C fan) for the filling; 190°C for blind baking the cases

content.text: Individual pumpkin pies are the dinner party version of the classic Thanksgiving centrepiece, each guest gets their own crisp tartlet with a smooth, spiced pumpkin custard. They bake at a low temperature so the custard stays silky rather than grainy. The spice blend here is the traditional American combination; add more or less as you prefer.

items.prepNote: pure pumpkin puree, not pie filling

content.text: Line and blind bake the tartlet cases

Make the pastry, chill for 30 minutes, then roll to 3 mm. Cut circles large enough to line eight 10 cm deep tartlet tins, pressing carefully into the corners. Trim the edges and refrigerate for 20 minutes. Blind bake at 190°C with beans for 12 minutes, then without for 8 minutes until dry and pale gold. Leave to cool.

Preheat the oven to 160°C conventional (140°C fan). Whisk together the pumpkin puree, cream, eggs, sugar, and spices until smooth. Pour into the blind-baked tartlet cases, filling to just below the rim. Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the custard is set with a slight wobble. Cool completely before serving, at least 1 hour. Serve with lightly whipped cream.
